An indirect question introduced by a wh-word takes no conjunction, so that must be dropped: the teacher asked who was absent.
Neither is singular, so the verb must be has done, not have done.
Recommend takes the subjunctive in the that-clause, so it must be that he reduce his expenditure, not that he would reduce.
In look forward to, the to is a preposition and must be followed by a gerund: to meeting you.
The reporting verb said is past, so the sequence of tenses requires would help rather than will help.
Reason takes for, not of: the reason for my absence. Insisted on knowing is correct.
Quotidian means everyday or daily, so in your quotidian life is used correctly, and the conditional wouldn't find with the prepositional phrase is sound. No part carries an error.
Dream of takes a gerund, so dreamed of being famous is correct, and in my prime is an idiomatic adverbial. No part carries an error.

Without an auxiliary the string is a fragment, so part (a) must read These shoes are designed. The competing reading would fault like yourself for like you, but the missing finite verb is the structural error.
An imperative joined to a following statement needs a coordinating conjunction, so part (b) must read any day and you will. As printed the two clauses run together without a link.
